metadata.title: Papyrus Component Definition
metadata.remarks: Describes the security capabilities of the Papyrus software and the responsibilities left to a deploying organization. It is not a certification, an authorization, an assessment result or a System Security Plan, and it makes no claim that any deployment satisfies NIST SP 800-53. Control effectiveness must be assessed within the deploying organization's authorization boundary. Evidence paths refer to the Papyrus source tree at the stated revision.

components.title: Papyrus
components.description: Papyrus is a single-tenant agent runtime that an organization deploys in its own environment as a FIPS-mode container image on Amazon Linux 2023 or an Azure VM appliance. It runs named, signed agents and workflows over the organization's documents and connected systems, signs people in through the organization's OpenID Connect provider (Microsoft Entra ID is one option), takes its configuration from a reviewable papyrus.yaml, keeps an append-only audit trail it can export over OTLP, and routes consequential external actions through human approval.

control-implementations.description: Papyrus contributions to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls, at revision a3d9ded116d8b3bee11c2ee6e9cd8b918566e720.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus creates no local user accounts or passwords; every person is an identity from the organization's OpenID Connect provider or Microsoft Entra ID, configured in papyrus.yaml, and authority comes only from the declared Papyrus roles, from token or directory-group claims mapped in papyrus.yaml, or from Papyrus role assignments. There is no first-run setup page: the first System Owners are named in papyrus.yaml (identity.owners) and receive the role when they first sign in. Only a System Owner (never an API key) can grant or revoke roles, the last System Owner cannot be revoked, and every grant and revocation is written to an append-only event table. With SCIM 2.0 provisioning on, a person the directory deprovisions or deactivates loses access on their next request. Automation uses API keys: service identities with no roles that name the workflows they may run and expire after 1 to 365 days (default 90).
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Own the account lifecycle in the identity provider (proofing, approval, periodic review, removal), name the first System Owners in papyrus.yaml, and review Papyrus role assignments and API keys on the organization's cadence.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (principalFromClaims and group mappings; grantConfiguredOwner grants identity.owners at sign-in; withDirectory checks SCIM status per request)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/role-assignments.ts` (Append-only role events, last-System-Owner guard)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/config.ts` (loadConfig refuses to start without an identity provider; no setup phase)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/api-keys.ts` (Workflow-scoped API keys: expiry, rotation, revocation, last use)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-auth.test.ts` (Maps only declared Entra app roles and never provisions local roles)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/api-keys.test.ts` (Key expiry, revocation, rotation, last-use recording and roleless service identity)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-role-assignments.test.ts` (Grants, lists and revokes assignments, never removes the last System Owner)

Known gap: A person who holds System Owner through a Papyrus role assignment keeps access while SCIM reports them deprovisioned (intended as break-glass), and there is no administrator action to end a person's active sessions. Remediation: Limit the SCIM bypass to accounts named in papyrus.yaml and audit each use; add a System Owner action to revoke a person's sessions.

implemented-requirements.description: Every protected HTTP route authenticates the caller server-side and rejects principals that hold no Papyrus role; administrative, integration, approval, audit and owner-only operations check the specific role on the server before acting. Until a System Owner accepts the current Terms of Service and Privacy Policy in the app, only sign-in, the terms and health routes answer. MCP servers, imported APIs and API keys are scoped to the caller's tenant, and an API key is admitted only to start runs of the workflows it names and read the runs it started. Named agents run only from an active, signed revision; within a session an agent may use any tool the deployment offers, and whether a tool call needs a person's approval is decided by the tool's permission policy and, for MCP tools, the administrator's classification.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Assign Papyrus roles in Entra according to organizational need-to-know.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (requireRole/requireAnyRole on routes; TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED gate (LEGAL_EXEMPT))
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/roster/store.ts` (assertSession requires an active signed revision; beforeTool enforces budgets)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/native-runtime.ts` (Tool permission policies (allow/ask) per tool and MCP classification)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-integrations.test.ts` (Integration operations require Entra application roles)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-observability.test.ts` (Rejects an authenticated user without an observability role)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-api-keys-http.test.ts` (API keys refused everywhere except starting and reading their own workflow runs)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-http.test.ts` (People without Integration.Manage see only verified servers and no settings)

Known gap: Agent sessions, their messages, the AgentFS Library and generated artifacts are owned by the tenant, not by the person who created them. Any signed-in person holding any Papyrus role can list and read every session, Library file and artifact in the deployment. Remediation: Record an owner on each session and Library namespace, enforce owner or explicit-share checks in the session, workspace-file and artifact routes, and add tests for cross-user denial.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus enforces fixed flow rules in code: agent workspace commands run with network access denied; repository imports and package installs are downloaded by the server, never the sandbox, and nothing in them runs; credentials are resolved by trusted runtime code and never passed to models or workspace processes; MCP tool results are labeled as external content. Outbound requests made for workflow HTTP steps, link previews, MCP servers and repository imports pass an egress gate: with egress.allowedHosts set in papyrus.yaml only listed hosts (names or *.suffix) are reached, and on the disconnected profile nothing outside the boundary is reached until it is listed.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_DENYLIST and PAPYRUS_WORKFLOW_HTTP_INTERNAL_HOSTS to match the authorization boundary, and enforce egress policy at the network layer.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/egress.ts` (assertEgressAllowed: allow-list, default deny on disconnected)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workflow-runtime-tools.ts` (Workflow HTTP targets checked against the gate)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/fetch-preview.ts` (Link previews checked against the gate)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/connect.ts` (MCP servers checked against the gate)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/repository-import.ts` (Every redirect hop checked; links and paths outside the target skipped)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-egress.test.ts` (Default deny on disconnected, listed hosts, wildcard matching)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-repository-import.test.ts` (Redirect hosts checked against the allow-list)

Known gap: Model gateway, identity provider discovery and Sentry connections do not pass the egress gate (they are configured endpoints), and the gate does not pin the resolved address, so a host that changes its DNS answer between check and connect could reach an internal address. Remediation: Route every outbound connection through the gate and connect to the address that was checked.

implemented-requirements.description: The agent can propose but cannot approve: approveProposal, denyProposal and executeAction are rejected at the agent tool layer, and approval routes require a human Entra session holding Papyrus.Action.Approve. Workflow approval steps addressed to a person or group can be answered only by that person, a member of that group, or a System Owner, never by the person who started the run. Authority-weakening policy changes wait for a Governance principal (System Owner, or Security.Manage plus Action.Approve).
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Assign Papyrus.Action.Approve, Papyrus.Security.Manage and Papyrus.System.Owner to different people according to organizational separation-of-duties policy.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/tools.ts` (FORBIDDEN_AGENT_TOOLS lists approveProposal, denyProposal, executeAction)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/workflow-approval.ts` (mayAnswerApproval: assigned approvals exclude the requester)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/store.ts` (requireGovernance and governed_changes approval)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/service.ts` (approveProposal requires Papyrus.Action.Approve)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/security-invariants.test.ts` (Keeps approval and execution out of the agent's tools)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/workflow-approval.test.ts` (Requester cannot approve their own addressed request, even as an approver)

Known gap: Action proposals and governed changes do not check that the approver differs from the person who proposed or requested them, so one person holding the approving roles can approve their own request. Unaddressed workflow approval steps can be answered by the run's initiator. Remediation: Refuse approval when the approver's object ID equals the proposer or requester for action proposals, governed changes and unaddressed workflow steps, with an explicit single-operator override recorded in the audit log.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus splits authority into roles (integration view and manage, security manage, action approve, audit view and system owner) and checks the narrowest one per operation; Papyrus.System.Owner implies all of them. API keys hold no roles. The container runs as a non-root user, and workspace commands run with the data directory unreadable and network denied.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Grant the narrowest role that fits each person, limit System Owner assignments, and do not run the container privileged.

- Evidence: `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` (ENTRA_APP_ROLES and OBSERVABILITY_APP_ROLES)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (hasAppRole: System Owner implies every role)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/entra-app-setup.ts` (Role descriptions declared on the Entra app)
- Evidence: `Dockerfile` (USER nonroot in the runtime stage)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-auth.test.ts` (System Owner role is treated as all portal permissions)

Known gap: Possession of any role, including narrow ones such as Papyrus.Audit.View, grants access to the shared agent workspace: all sessions, chat, Library files and artifacts. Workspace access is not itself a separately assignable privilege. Remediation: Introduce a distinct workspace-use role or per-session ownership (see ac-3) so that narrow roles do not carry workspace access.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus accepts no passwords, so interactive logon attempts and lockout are handled by the identity provider. Every completed and failed sign-in callback is written to the audit trail with the client address. Workflow webhook secrets are 256 random bits made by the server, and invalid, expired, revoked and rotated API keys all receive the same 401.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Configure Entra smart lockout, Conditional Access and sign-in risk policies for the tenant.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (auth.sign_in success and failure audit records on the OIDC/Entra callback)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/api-keys.ts` (Uniform 401 for bad keys)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-workflow-webhook-http.test.ts` (Bad and missing signatures get 401; a rotated-away secret stops working)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-api-keys-http.test.ts` (Missing, malformed, revoked or rotated-away keys get the same answer)

implemented-requirements.description: With security.notice set in papyrus.yaml, Papyrus shows the system use notice before sign-in (dow for the standard DoD notice and consent banner, or the organization's own text from a file) and starts sign-in only after the person consents. Each acknowledgement is recorded in the audit trail with the notice's digest and the client address.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Choose the notice text approved for the system and set security.notice.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (DOW_NOTICE, systemNotice; login refused without the acknowledged digest; auth.notice_acknowledged record)
- Evidence: `apps/web/src/App.tsx` (Notice screen before the sign-in button)

implemented-requirements.description: Each person may hold at most three portal sessions at once by default (security.sessions.concurrent); a new sign-in ends the oldest beyond the limit.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set the limit the organization requires.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/portal-sessions.ts` (open() ends sessions beyond the concurrent limit)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-portal-sessions.test.ts` (Oldest session ended at the limit)

implemented-requirements.description: After 15 minutes without activity (security.sessions.idleMinutes) the portal signs the person out and returns to the sign-in screen, and the server ends the session independently, so an unattended browser requires re-authentication through the identity provider.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Apply operating-system screen locks on endpoints.

- Evidence: `apps/web/src/App.tsx` (Idle timer signs out at the configured limit)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/portal-sessions.ts` (Server-side idle limit)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-portal-sessions.test.ts` (Idle session ends and cannot be reopened)

implemented-requirements.description: Portal sessions are recorded on the server. Each sign-in opens a session that ends after 15 minutes without activity, after 12 hours however active it is, or on sign-out, which ends it on the server so a copied cookie stops working (security.sessions in papyrus.yaml sets the limits). The signed cookie carries only the session identifier and identity; each request is checked against the session record, and ending a session is audited.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set identity-provider token lifetimes and sign-in frequency; choose session limits in papyrus.yaml that meet the organization's policy.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/portal-sessions.ts` (Server-side sessions: idle limit, maximum lifetime, concurrent cap, end on sign-out)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (Cookie carries the session id; each request is checked; auth.session_end audited)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-portal-sessions.test.ts` (Idle, maximum lifetime, sign-out replay and concurrent cap)

implemented-requirements.description: With security.classification set in papyrus.yaml, every screen, including sign-in and the Terms page, carries the system-high classification banner at the top in the standard colours (UNCLASSIFIED through TOP SECRET//SCI).
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set the system-high classification; apply marking to documents and media under the organization's marking policy.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (classification published in /api/config/public)
- Evidence: `apps/web/src/App.tsx` (ClassificationBanner on every screen)
- Evidence: `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` (CLASSIFICATION_BANNERS colours and labels)

Known gap: Files Papyrus generates (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, exports) are not marked, and records carry no per-item classification. Remediation: Stamp the system-high marking on generated files and exports.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus writes one append-only audit trail of security events: successful and failed sign-ins, sign-outs, sessions ended for inactivity or age, acknowledgement of the system use notice, every refused request (401 and 403) with its route, acceptance of the Terms, and audit export tests. Separate append-only records cover role grants and revocations, every MCP tool call and MCP administrative change, API key lifecycle, policy decisions, configuration at each start, integration and action-ledger events, and agent signatures and evidence.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Decide which additional events the organization requires and collect Entra sign-in logs from Microsoft.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/audit/log.ts` (papyrus_audit_events: one schema, append-only)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (Sign-in, sign-out, notice, terms and access.denied records)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (Session end records)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/calls.ts` (MCP call records)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-integrations.test.ts` (Lifecycle events are appended and the chain verifies)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-stores.test.ts` (Records who classified an MCP tool)

Known gap: Document downloads, session and workflow deletions, and agent tool calls are recorded in their own stores or not at all, rather than in the unified audit trail. Remediation: Write these events to the unified audit trail.

implemented-requirements.description: Unified audit records carry a sequence number, an ISO 8601 UTC time, the action, the outcome (success, failure or denied), the actor and the person an agent acted for, the target, the client network address, user agent, request ID and session ID, and event detail without secrets or document content. MCP call records add session, workflow, tool classification, approval ID, duration and a SHA-256 of the arguments.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/audit/log.ts` (AuditEvent fields; auditRequest takes the socket address, never a forwarded header)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-local-secrets.test.ts` (Key create/replace/delete does not leak secret values into audit events)

implemented-requirements.description: Audit records are kept in the Papyrus data directory and, when audit.otlp is configured, delivered to the organization's collector; records written while the collector is unreachable are sent when it returns, and the backlog is shown on the Audit page.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Size the data volume and the collector's storage for the retention period the organization requires.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/audit/otlp.ts` (Durable export cursor and backlog)

Known gap: Papyrus does not watch free space on the data volume or alert when it runs low. Remediation: Add capacity monitoring and an alert.

implemented-requirements.description: System Owners and Audit Viewers review the trail on the Audit page: search by person or action, filter by outcome and time range, read each record in full, and export the filtered list as CSV or JSONL. The same records are sent to the organization's OpenTelemetry collector (OTLP/HTTP, with optional CA and mutual TLS) for review in its SIEM, at least once, resuming after an outage; the page shows the export's health and can send a test record.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set review cadence, alerting and escalation, and correlate Papyrus records with Entra and host logs in the organization's monitoring system.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/audit/otlp.ts` (OTLP exporter: durable cursor, retry with backoff, TLS and mTLS)
- Evidence: `apps/web/src/Audit.tsx` (Audit page: filters, detail, CSV/JSONL export, export status)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (/api/audit/* require System Owner or Audit View; API keys refused)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-audit-otlp.test.ts` (Records exported once, with headers, resuming after a collector failure)

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus writes audit timestamps as ISO 8601 UTC strings taken from the host clock.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Synchronize the host clock to an authoritative time source.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/role-assignments.ts` (new Date().toISOString() on each event)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/calls.ts` (Call timestamps in ISO 8601 UTC)

implemented-requirements.description: Audit tables are append-only at the database layer: triggers abort UPDATE and DELETE on the unified audit trail and on role, configuration, MCP, integration and model event tables; integration and action-ledger events are additionally SHA-256 hash-chained. With OTLP export configured, every record is also held by a collector outside the Papyrus host.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Restrict host and database-file access, protect backups, and copy audit records to independently controlled immutable storage.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/database.ts` (No-update/no-delete triggers and verifyEventChain)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/calls.ts` (Append-only triggers on papyrus_mcp_calls)
- Evidence: `docs/security.md` (States that a host or database administrator can replace local state)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-integrations.test.ts` (verifyEventChain reports a valid chain after lifecycle changes)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-smoke.test.ts` (Event chain verifies after an end-to-end run)

Known gap: Triggers detect changes made through the application only; anyone with write access to the database file can rewrite local records, and the unified trail is not hash-chained or signed. Off-host export mitigates this only when configured. Remediation: Chain and sign the unified trail with a key held outside the data directory and verify it on a schedule; require OTLP export on classified deployments.

implemented-requirements.description: Audit records are generated server-side at the enforcement points themselves: the proposal approval and denial paths, the single MCP call path, role assignment changes, API key management and policy enforcement. They are therefore produced the same way regardless of which client made the request.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/service.ts` (approveProposal and denyProposal call recordActionEvent)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/calls.ts` (executeMcpTool writes start and finish records around every call)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/store.ts` (assert records each denial in policy_decisions)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-integrations.test.ts` (Event count and chain after integration operations)

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus ships one container image: Amazon Linux 2023 minimal with OpenSSL's certified FIPS provider forced on, running as a non-root user with no browser engine, scanned in CI against the DISA STIG profile for Amazon Linux 2023. Runtime configuration comes from papyrus.yaml, a reviewable file in which secrets appear only as file or environment references, and its digest and effective settings are recorded at every start. Three deployment profiles (commercial, government, disconnected) set network posture.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Document the approved deployment configuration: host OS, network, Entra registration, model endpoint, storage and the Papyrus image digest.

- Evidence: `Dockerfile` (Build and runtime stages, nonroot user, dod target)
- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/provision.sh` (Appliance provisioning, loopback port binding, nginx TLS edge)
- Evidence: `docs/deployment.md` (Deployment profiles and required settings)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-image-and-catalog.test.ts` (Keeps Chromium and agent-browser out of the hardened core image)

Known gap: The baseline is not fully reproducible: base images are referenced by tag rather than digest, apk packages are not version-pinned, and several Python packages in the runtime image (pypdf, pypdfium2, reportlab, pillow) are unpinned. Remediation: Pin base images by digest and pin apk and pip package versions, with an automated update process that opens reviewed changes.

implemented-requirements.description: In-application changes that weaken policy become digest-checked governed changes that apply only after a Governance principal approves them, and an approval is refused if the change's digest or expected version no longer matches. Papyrus software updates are announced by exact image digest from an allowed repository and installed only when a System Owner applies them or within an owner-configured maintenance window.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Operate organizational change control for deployment configuration, infrastructure and when updates are applied.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/store.ts` (propose/approve with digest and expected-version checks)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/updates/service.ts` (Digest-only releases from allowed repositories; apply only the announced release)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/http.ts` (/api/governed-changes approval route)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-policies.test.ts` (Approved change commits atomically; a stale approval is rolled back without relaxing rules)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-updates.test.ts` (Accepts only exact digests from allowed repositories and applies only when asked or in the window)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-policies-http.test.ts` (A relaxation waits as a governed change and applies only on approval)

implemented-requirements.description: Configuration endpoints require specific roles on the server: Integration.Manage for model gateways, MCP servers, imported APIs, package mirrors, browser and mainframe settings and branding; System Owner for role assignments, updates, license activation and skill approval; Governance for governed changes. Model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Control access to the host, container runtime, data directory, secret stores and deployment pipeline.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (requireRole checks on configuration routes; requireSecretTransport)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/store.ts` (requireGovernance)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-updates.test.ts` (Only admins see and configure updates)

implemented-requirements.description: Configuration is validated at startup and fails closed: papyrus.yaml is checked against its schema (unknown keys and bad values stop startup), an identity provider is required, persistent mode requires an HTTPS public origin, the license named in license.file must verify for this deployment, and the former development and license bypasses are refused. Every start records which file was used, its digest and each effective setting with where it came from, and flags a change from the previous start.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Choose values appropriate to the authorization boundary and verify them at deployment. In Azure Government or other national clouds, set PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_ENDPOINT, PAPYRUS_AZURE_MANAGEMENT_RESOURCE, PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_DNS_SUFFIX and PAPYRUS_AZURE_KEYVAULT_RESOURCE; they default to Azure commercial endpoints and are not derived from PAPYRUS_ENTRA_CLOUD.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/config-file.ts` (papyrus.yaml schema and loader)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/config-audit.ts` (Configuration recorded at each start)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/index.ts` (license.file activated at startup or startup stops)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-config-origin.test.ts` (HTTPS configured origin is authoritative over Host headers)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/security-invariants.test.ts` (Government cloud selection explicit; unknown sandbox backends rejected)

implemented-requirements.description: The runtime image contains no browser engine. The Papyrus agent has no general shell: native programs run only through structured executors (Python, Pandoc, LibreOffice) with fixed executables. MCP has no stdio transport. The public scheduler CRUD surface is not exposed, and removed legacy connectors read back as retired and cannot be activated or executed.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Expose only ports 80/443 (and SSH if needed), and disable integrations and model endpoints the organization does not use.

- Evidence: `Dockerfile` (Runtime stage installs no Chromium or agent-browser)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workspace-executors.ts` (Structured executors with fixed executables)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/servers.ts` (Server addresses must be HTTP(S) URLs; no stdio)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/database.ts` (Rows for removed connectors read as retired)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-image-and-catalog.test.ts` (No Chromium or agent-browser in the core image; removed connectors are retired)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-workspace.test.ts` (Process execution kept behind structured executors)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-stores.test.ts` (Refuses stdio and private addresses)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-http.test.ts` (Scheduler portal APIs are not exposed)

implemented-requirements.description: A generator produces an SPDX 2.3 SBOM of every package in the pnpm lockfile, checked for drift by the pre-commit hook, and the container workflow generates a CycloneDX SBOM of the built image.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Inventory the host OS, container runtime, reverse proxy, model endpoints and other infrastructure in the boundary.

- Evidence: `scripts/compliance/generate.mjs` (SPDX SBOM generation from pnpm-lock.yaml)
- Evidence: `compliance/sbom.spdx.json` (Generated source SBOM)
- Evidence: `.github/workflows/container.yml` (anchore/sbom-action CycloneDX image SBOM)

Known gap: The SPDX SBOM records name and version only (licenses and download locations are NOASSERTION) and omits OS and Python packages; the image SBOM is not attached to the published image as a signed attestation. Remediation: Publish the image SBOM as a signed attestation alongside the provenance attestation and include license data.

implemented-requirements.description: Release images are signed with Cosign keyless signing in GitHub Actions. On the Azure Marketplace appliance the updater runs cosign verify against a pinned signer identity and issuer before pulling an update and installs nothing if verification fails; the Marketplace image pipeline verifies the signature and build provenance of the container digest before baking it.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: On self-hosted deployments, verify the image signature and digest before deployment.

- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/papyrus-update.sh` (cosign verify with PAPYRUS_UPDATE_SIGNER_IDENTITY before install)
- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/provision.sh` (Pinned cosign binary checksum and signer identity)
- Evidence: `.github/workflows/marketplace-vm-image.yml` (Verifies Cosign signature and attestation of the source image)
- Evidence: `.github/workflows/container.yml` (cosign sign and attest-build-provenance on push to main)
- Evidence: `deploy/azure/main.bicep` (Azure template references ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus:0.1.1 by tag)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-updates.test.ts` (Update service accepts only exact digests from allowed repositories)

Known gap: Signature verification exists only on the Marketplace VM update and image-build paths; the shell updater has no automated test, and other deployment paths do not verify signatures in this repository. The Azure template (deploy/azure/main.bicep) references ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus:0.1.1 by tag, a different repository from the one CI publishes (ghcr.io/beaglabs/papyrus/papyrus). Two workflows (container.yml and container-multiarch.yml) sign images for the same repository while the updater trusts only the container.yml identity. Remediation: Settle on one signing workflow and identity, reference images by digest from the published repository in every deployment template, add an automated test for the updater verification step, and document signature verification for every supported deployment path.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus keeps its state in the data directory (agent.db, mastra.db, jobs.db, observability.db, secrets.db and AgentFS) and documents which files must be backed up together and that the local master key must be backed up separately. It provides no backup tooling.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Back up the data directory consistently, store the master key and Key Vault recovery separately, and test restoration.

- Evidence: `docs/deployment.md` (Lists the databases to back up and master key handling)

implemented-requirements.description: People authenticate only through the organization's OpenID Connect provider or Microsoft Entra ID. Before sign-in starts, a configured system use notice must be acknowledged. Sign-in uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256), single-use state and a nonce; ID tokens are verified against the provider's published keys for issuer, audience, expiry and nonce. Multi-factor and PIV/CAC requirements are enforced by the identity provider, not by Papyrus.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Require MFA or phishing-resistant authentication through Entra Conditional Access.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (startLogin, completeLogin, verifyEntraToken, completeBrokeredLogin)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-auth-profile.test.ts` (Interactive login requests the expected scopes per national cloud)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-api-keys-http.test.ts` (An API key is not accepted as an Entra sign-in)

Known gap: Papyrus does not itself require multi-factor or certificate-based authentication (it trusts the identity provider's policy) and cannot accept client certificates (CAC/PIV or SIPR tokens) directly. Remediation: Optionally require MFA or smart-card authentication methods in the token (amr/acr), and support mutual TLS with NSS PKI where the enclave requires it.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus identifies people by Entra object ID and tenant ID and creates no identifiers of its own for people. API keys receive a random 12-hex-character identifier, and each deployment has its own deployment ID.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Manage identifier issuance and reuse policy in Entra ID.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (principalFromClaims requires oid and tid)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/api-keys.ts` (Random key identifiers)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-auth.test.ts` (Identity derived from Entra claims only)

implemented-requirements.description: API key secrets are 32 random bytes, shown once with cache-control no-store, and stored only as an HMAC-SHA-256 keyed with the deployment secret, so a copied database cannot be used to call the API. Keys expire, can be rotated (the old secret stops immediately) and revoked. Integration settings reject inline passwords, tokens and keys and store only credential references, and model API keys are accepted only over HTTPS from the portal origin. The pre-commit hook scans staged changes for private keys and common token formats.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Manage Entra authenticators (MFA methods, certificates, client secrets) and rotate API keys on the organization's schedule.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/api-keys.ts` (Secret generation, HMAC storage, expiry, rotation and revocation)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/service.ts` (rejectInlineSecrets on integration settings)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (requireSecretTransport for model API keys)
- Evidence: `scripts/hooks/secret-scan.mjs` (Pre-commit secret pattern scan)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/api-keys.test.ts` (Secret shown once and not stored; useless under another deployment secret; expiry, rotation, revocation)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-integrations.test.ts` (Rejects inline connector secrets and stores only references)

implemented-requirements.description: Only tokens issued for the bound Entra tenant are accepted, so any external person must exist in that tenant (for example as a guest). The only unauthenticated route for other systems is a workflow webhook (/hooks/<id>): it answers only for a published workflow with a webhook trigger, requires a signature made with the server-generated secret, and only starts that workflow with the event as its input.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Decide whether guests may be assigned Papyrus roles, and which workflows other systems may start by webhook.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (WRONG_ENTRA_TENANT check)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/workflow-webhooks.ts` (Constant-time signature check with 300-second tolerance; one run per event id)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-workflow-webhook-http.test.ts` (Signed event starts exactly one run; bad signature 401; unpublished workflow 404)

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus provides no incident handling capability or plan. Its audit and observability records are inputs to the deploying organization's process.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Deploying organization: Maintain and exercise an incident response plan covering the Papyrus deployment, including revoking roles, API keys and connector credentials and preserving audit databases.

implemented-requirements.description: CI scans each built image against the DISA STIG SCAP profile for Amazon Linux 2023, and the published evidence pack includes Trivy vulnerability scans of every platform of the released image. Dependency and static-analysis scanning do not run in CI.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Scan hosts, the deployed image and surrounding infrastructure with the organization's tools.

- Evidence: `.github/workflows/container.yml` (Generates an image SBOM; contains no scanning step)

Known gap: No dependency or static-analysis scanning runs in CI, and there are no severity-based remediation timeframes. Remediation: Add dependency and code scanning to CI and publish remediation timeframes.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus calls no Beag Labs service: licenses are verified locally against keys built into Papyrus, sign-in uses the organization's own identity provider, and the Terms and Privacy Policy ship inside the app. Sentry error reporting is off unless a DSN is set and runs with sendDefaultPii disabled.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Assess the configured model gateway, MCP servers and any Sentry DSN as external services.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/license.ts` (Local signature verification against the built-in license authorities)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/sentry.ts` (Sentry initialized only with a DSN, sendDefaultPii false)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-license-authorities.test.ts` (Only the built-in authorities verify licenses)

implemented-requirements.description: The repository has workspace-wide TypeScript type checking and a Vitest suite for the server covering identity, authorization, MCP, secrets, sandboxing and approvals. CI runs type checking and a fixed subset of tests (scoped workflows, mainframe guardrails, policies, execution records, channel linking and offline evaluations), and a local pre-commit hook runs secret, contract and compliance-drift checks plus security-invariant tests when related files change.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (CI typecheck and the tests it runs)
- Evidence: `scripts/hooks/precommit.mjs` (Pre-commit checks and conditional test runs)
- Evidence: `apps/server/tests/security-invariants.test.ts` (Security invariant tests)

Known gap: Most security tests, including identity, MCP and Key Vault tests, do not run in CI, and the compliance drift check runs only in the local pre-commit hook, which can be skipped. compliance/ssp.md states that these checks run in CI. Remediation: Run the full server test suite and pnpm compliance:check in CI on every pull request and make them required checks.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus databases are opened with SQLite secure_delete, so content removed from them is overwritten rather than left in free pages. Each agent workspace runs in its own sandboxed process with a temporary materialized workspace.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Use volume encryption and sanitize media under the organization's procedures.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/database.ts` (secure_delete on agent.db)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/runtime.ts` (secure_delete on session and trace stores)

Known gap: Deleting a session does not remove every copy of its content (workspace files, traces, embeddings), and there is no administrator purge for spillage. Remediation: Add a cascading purge with verification.

implemented-requirements.description: Request bodies are read under fixed byte ceilings and refused with 413 beyond them; workflow webhooks are rate-limited per webhook and take bodies of at most 1 MB; pending sign-ins are capped; and outbound workflow requests time out after 15 seconds with bodies limited to 256 KiB.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Provide network-layer DoS protection and rate limiting at the reverse proxy or gateway.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (body() and rawBody() byte limits)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/rate-limit.ts` (MinuteRateLimiter)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/workflow-webhooks.ts` (Per-webhook delivery limit)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-http.test.ts` (Refuses an oversized chat body)

Known gap: Rate limits are in memory and keyed on the socket address; behind the appliance's nginx proxy every client shares one address, and the limiter clears all windows once it tracks 10,000 keys. The cap of 256 pending sign-ins can be exhausted by unauthenticated requests, blocking sign-in for up to 10 minutes. Remediation: Key limits on a trusted forwarded client address, bound memory without clearing all windows, and rate-limit /api/auth/entra/login per client instead of a global cap.

implemented-requirements.description: Workflow HTTP steps, link previews, MCP servers and repository imports pass one egress gate: HTTPS, no embedded credentials, refusal of hosts that resolve to loopback, private or link-local addresses unless listed as internal, and, when egress.allowedHosts is set (required on the disconnected profile), only listed hosts. Redirects are re-checked hop by hop. Workspace commands have no network access. On the Marketplace appliance the container is published only on 127.0.0.1 behind nginx.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Place the deployment behind the organization's firewalls and proxies, restrict inbound access to 443, and set the egress denylist and internal-host list.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workflow-runtime-tools.ts` (assertWorkflowHttpTarget)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/oauth.ts` (mcpFetch applies the same check and redirect: manual)
- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/provision.sh` (docker run -p 127.0.0.1:${PAPYRUS_PORT}; nginx proxy)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/azure-key-vault.ts` (Deployment vault created with publicNetworkAccess Enabled)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/workflow-http-target.test.ts` (Address classification, denylist and internal-host rules)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-stores.test.ts` (Refuses private addresses and plain HTTP to public hosts)

Known gap: The address check resolves DNS separately from the connection that follows, so a host that changes its DNS answer between the two can reach an internal address. The deployment Key Vault is created with public network access enabled. Remediation: Connect to the address that was checked (pinned lookup) for all outbound requests, and support private endpoints or firewall rules for the deployment Key Vault.

implemented-requirements.description: Persistent mode refuses to start without an HTTPS public origin. The daemon can terminate TLS itself with a TLS 1.2 minimum, and the Marketplace appliance's nginx edge allows only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 and sends HSTS. Portal cookies are Secure under HTTPS. Outbound connections to MCP servers, workflows and imported APIs require HTTPS except for hosts the organization explicitly lists as internal.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Provide certificates, TLS termination and cipher policy that meet organizational requirements.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/config.ts` (Persistent deployments require an HTTPS PAPYRUS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (createHttpsServer with minVersion TLSv1.2)
- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/provision.sh` (ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 and HSTS)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/workflow-http-target.test.ts` (Rejects plain HTTP to non-internal hosts)

implemented-requirements.description: The local secrets master key must be a separately provisioned 32-byte file that is not group- or world-writable and is opened without following symlinks; the server never generates it. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, the portal secret, Entra client secret and model and provider keys are kept in a deployment Key Vault (RBAC mode, purge protection, 90-day soft delete) with only the VM's managed identity granted access, and each reader is limited to its own secret-name prefix. License authority public keys are supplied by configuration or baked into the DoD image.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Provision, back up and protect the master key and portal secret; manage Entra and TLS keys.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/local-secrets.ts` (Master key checks)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/deployment-vault.ts` (Core vault and purpose-prefix read guard)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/azure-key-vault.ts` (Vault properties and single role assignment)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/openapi/credentials.ts` (Connector credential key derived as SHA-256 of the portal secret)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-local-secrets.test.ts` (Fails closed with missing, insecure or incorrect master keys)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-deployment-vault.test.ts` (Each caller reads only its own secrets; references refused without an Azure identity)

Known gap: There is no rotation or key-versioning support for the portal secret or the local master key. Encryption keys for connector credentials are derived with a single SHA-256 of the portal secret, so changing that secret makes stored values unreadable. The Key Vault uses the Standard (software-protected) tier. Remediation: Introduce versioned data-encryption keys with a proper KDF, a re-encryption procedure for rotation, and an option for HSM-backed keys.

implemented-requirements.description: The image runs OpenSSL with Amazon Linux 2023's certified FIPS 140-3 provider (CMVP #5438) forced on, and Papyrus refuses to start if FIPS mode is not active or MD5 is still allowed. Stored credentials use AES-256-GCM; cookies, API key hashes and webhook signatures use HMAC-SHA-256; hash chains use SHA-256.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Where FIPS 140 validated cryptography is required, run on a validated module and terminate TLS on validated infrastructure.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/fips-check.ts` (Startup refuses to run unless getFips() is 1 and MD5 is refused)
- Evidence: `Dockerfile` (AL2023 with openssl-fips-provider-certified, FIPS forced)

Known gap: Signatures and MACs use P-256 and SHA-256 rather than the CNSA suite (P-384, SHA-384) that national security systems may require. Remediation: Move Papyrus-generated signatures and MACs to CNSA algorithms while still verifying existing ones.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus runs no agent-built code in the browser. HTML and SVG artifacts are served as attachments with a sandbox CSP (default-src 'none'), so they cannot run in the portal's origin.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (Active artifact content served as attachment with sandbox CSP)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-artifact-content-http.test.ts` (HTML artifacts are sandboxed attachments; passive content is inline)

implemented-requirements.description: The portal session cookie is HMAC-SHA-256 signed with the deployment secret, compared in constant time, and set HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure and with the __Host- prefix under HTTPS. OIDC state and nonce are random 32-byte values held server-side, single-use and expiring after 10 minutes; MCP OAuth sign-ins are likewise single-use, bound to the initiating person and checked against the discovered issuer. Once an HTTPS origin is configured, request headers cannot change the origin used for redirects or cookies.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/auth.ts` (portalCookie, verifyPortalCookie, pending login state)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mcp/oauth.ts` (10-minute single-use pending sign-ins with issuer check)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/config.ts` (deriveOrigin)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-runtime.test.ts` (Refuses a callback from another person, a reused state and a different issuer)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-config-origin.test.ts` (HTTPS origin authoritative over Host headers)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-auth-profile.test.ts` (Signed cookie carries only the authority-bearing identity)

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus encrypts secrets at the application layer with AES-256-GCM and per-record associated data: model gateway keys in a separate 0600 secrets database under a separately provisioned master key; and connector, imported-API and MCP credentials bound to their owner. Where Azure Key Vault is configured, platform secrets are stored there and configuration files hold only references. SQLite databases are opened with secure_delete, so deleted rows are overwritten rather than left in free pages.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Encrypt the volume that holds the data directory and its backups, and manage those keys.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/local-secrets.ts` (secrets.db encryption and file permissions)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/openapi/credentials.ts` (Owner-bound AES-256-GCM connector credentials)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/deployment-vault.ts` (Key Vault storage of platform secrets)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-local-secrets.test.ts` (Encrypted persistence, tamper rejection and cross-profile binding)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-stores.test.ts` (Shared MCP token stored encrypted and never returned)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-deployment-vault.test.ts` (bootstrap.json holds only references)

Known gap: Agent sessions, Library documents, audit records and traces are stored in unencrypted SQLite and AgentFS files; their confidentiality at rest depends on volume encryption the deploying organization provides. Remediation: Require and verify an encrypted volume for the data directory on classified deployments.

implemented-requirements.description: Commands the Papyrus agent runs in its workspace run in a separate worker process under landstrip (Landlock and seccomp on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS) with writes limited to a temporary materialized workspace, the Papyrus data directory unreadable and network denied. The worker validates and resolves the effective policy before starting the command and refuses to run if the write root, network restriction or data-directory denial is not in effect; unsupported platforms run no workspace commands. Credential-like environment variables are removed before the command starts.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Run on a Linux host with Landlock enabled and do not run the container privileged.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workspace-nono-worker.ts` (landstrip policy, validate/resolve checks, fail-closed exits)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workspace-nono.ts` (Worker launch and sensitiveEnvironmentKey stripping)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/mastra/workspace-landstrip.ts` (Read-confinement check of the resolved policy)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/security-invariants.test.ts` (Fails closed without OS isolation; strips credential-like environment values; rejects cwd traversal)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-workspace.test.ts` (Reports landstrip isolation and refuses escaping working directories)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-session-workspace.test.ts` (Rejects snapshots that include daemon data or parent roots)

implemented-requirements.description: Beag Labs publishes fixes as new signed images. A deployment learns of a release through an HMAC-signed, timestamped webhook with replay protection, and a System Owner applies it or allows it to apply within a maintenance window; the Marketplace updater verifies the image signature before installing.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Set patch windows, test updates and apply them within organizational timeframes.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/updates/service.ts` (verifyWebhook, announce, apply, maintenance window)
- Evidence: `deploy/marketplace/vm/papyrus-update.sh` (Signature verification and install)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-updates.test.ts` (Signature over timestamp and body, replay refusal, window-limited auto-apply)

Known gap: Beag Labs has no documented flaw remediation timeframes by severity, and no published security advisory or vulnerability disclosure process (no SECURITY.md). Remediation: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy and severity-based remediation SLAs, and announce fixed vulnerabilities in release notes.

implemented-requirements.description: Papyrus records agent traces and logs in a separate observability database readable by System Owners, Audit Viewers and Security Managers, writes structured JSON warnings to standard output, and can send errors to a customer-supplied Sentry DSN. Security events are written to the unified audit trail and exported to the organization's collector over OTLP when configured. The container health check verifies that the landstrip sandbox enforces its boundary; it does not check that the HTTP service is answering.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Collect container output and audit data into the organization's monitoring platform and alert on it.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (Observability trace and log routes)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/sentry.ts` (Optional Sentry reporting)
- Evidence: `Dockerfile` (HEALTHCHECK)
- Evidence: `deploy/container/healthcheck.mjs` (Health check probes landstrip write confinement only)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-observability.test.ts` (Role-gated access to traces and logs)

implemented-requirements.description: Releases are referenced by image digest and signature-verified before the Marketplace updater installs them. Governed changes are re-hashed at approval and refused if the digest differs. Integration and action events are hash-chained.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Verify image digests and signatures on deployment paths other than the Marketplace appliance.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/updates/service.ts` (Exact digest references only)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/store.ts` (CHANGE_TAMPERED digest check)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-policies.test.ts` (Stale approvals roll back)

implemented-requirements.description: Request bodies must be JSON objects under per-route byte limits; required strings are length-bounded; policy rules are validated against a fixed schema; outbound addresses are validated before use; and workflow webhook payloads are signature-checked over the exact raw bytes before they are parsed.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (body(), rawBody(), requiredString(), boundedInteger())
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/policies/evaluator.ts` (validateRules)
- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/workflow-webhooks.ts` (verifyWebhook over the raw body)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-policies.test.ts` (Fails closed for missing context and invalid rules)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-http.test.ts` (Bounds session IDs and chat bodies)

implemented-requirements.description: Errors are returned as JSON with a code and a per-request ID. Known error types map to specific status codes, sign-in error pages do not echo request input, the browser connection address is masked in error text, and imported-API credentials are redacted from errors.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Configure log handling so diagnostic output is not exposed beyond administrators.

- Evidence: `apps/server/src/agent/http.ts` (Central error mapping with requestId; INTERNAL_ERROR branch)
- Verified by: `apps/server/tests/agent-mcp-http.test.ts` (A cancelled sign-in page does not echo anything from the address)

Known gap: Unexpected exceptions are returned to the client as 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with the exception's message text, which can disclose internal details. Remediation: Return a generic message for unmapped errors and log the detail server-side under the request ID.

implemented-requirements.description: Container images built from main are signed with Cosign and receive a GitHub build provenance attestation. Dependencies are locked in pnpm-lock.yaml and installed with --frozen-lockfile in CI, and the pnpm version is pinned with a hash in packageManager.
implemented-requirements.remarks:
Deploying organization: Retain the image digests and attestations for deployed releases and verify them at intake.

- Evidence: `.github/workflows/container.yml` (cosign sign and actions/attest-build-provenance)
- Evidence: `pnpm-lock.yaml` (Locked dependency graph)
- Evidence: `package.json` (packageManager pnpm pinned with hash)
- Evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile)

Known gap: GitHub Actions are referenced by mutable version tags rather than commit SHAs, and base images and OS and Python packages in the Dockerfile are not pinned, so build inputs are not fully traceable. Remediation: Pin all Actions to commit SHAs and pin image and package inputs (see cm-2), recording them in the provenance attestation.
